subject: Customer lifeline bridge + comm playbook — Horizon Health latency & 5xx spike
messages:
Date: 2027-05-18T09:03:00-07:00
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Subject: URGENT: Horizon Health — sustained latency & 5xx spike (production)

Team —

Monitoring picked up a sustained increase in p95 latency (from ~180ms to ~1.2s) and a correlated spike in 5xx error rate for Horizon Health (prod-us-west) starting ~08:40 PDT. Traffic patterns look normal; request volume is within expected ranges. The incident is affecting several high-throughput routes (chat.generate and embeddings.bulk). Horizon has reported timeouts in their ingestion pipeline.

I’ve attached a small request sample and a short NVML dump (nvml-stacktrace.txt) that the infra agent captured. Key asks up front:
- We need a decision on invoking an exec bridge now — customer is asking for an ETA and potential credits.
- Assign mitigation owners (runtime patch / scale / routing fallbacks).
- Draft customer-facing update within 60 minutes.

I’m standing up a short bridge at 09:20 PDT: https://zoom.us/j/987654321 — please join if you can.

Marcus
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: nvml-stacktrace.txt (log excerpt), request-sample-1678.json (sample payload)

From: Kevin Jansen <kevin.jansen@horizonhealth.com>

Can you confirm whether this is a platform-wide issue and when we can expect normal service? Also please advise on SLA credit eligibility — this is affecting our busiest hour.

Kevin Jansen
VP Engineering, Horizon Health
kevin.jansen@horizonhealth.com

Date: 2027-05-18T09:21:00-07:00
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren.bishop@lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Subject: RE: URGENT: Horizon Health — sustained latency & 5xx spike (production)

Joining bridge now. Quick plan proposal (to agree on during bridge):
1) Triage (Ben) — confirm JVM/GPU telemetry and kernel traces; isolate whether this is NVML/driver related or model runtime regression.
2) Mitigate (Grace) — temporarily route Horizon traffic to cold-hot pool with conservative batching; enable prefix/KV cache warming for their top request IDs.
3) Capacity (Marcus) — add two instances to Horizon's dedicated pool (reserved capacity) and open autoscale burst (if available).
4) Customer comms (Lauren) — draft and send an interim status update, include ETA window of 2–3 hours for full mitigation and potential SLA credit language.

Please assign and confirm in the bridge. If we escalate to exec (C-level) we’ll keep the bridge but send a 1-sentence summary to the exec chain.

V

Bridge: https://zoom.us/j/987654321 (09:20 PDT)
Attendees: Marcus, Vanessa, Ben, Grace, Lauren, Horizon support (Kevin)

(Note: I captured a timeline screenshot in Drive: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/11wQ-status-logs)

Date: 2027-05-18T10:04:00-07:00
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Subject: Re: URGENT: Horizon Health — sustained latency & 5xx spike (production) — root cause & mitigations

Quick root-cause update from infra diagnostics: we’re seeing repeated NVML timeouts and a leaking driver thread that results in KV cache churn and long tail GC pauses on the model host machines. Symptoms line up with the NVML stacktrace I attached earlier.

Actions taken (10:00 PDT):
- Rolled the model hosts to a previous NVML driver (v495 -> v490) on a canary subset — latency p95 dropped by ~40% for that block.
- Enabled aggressive prefix/KV cache retention for Horizon’s routes to reduce cold-KV misses.
- Temporarily increased Horizon’s dedicated pool by +2 instances and bumped their burst posture.
- Added a routing policy to send large-request bursts to a lower-cost compatible variant to avoid backpressure on the primary pool.

Next steps (owners):
- Grace: complete KV cache warm-up script and validate on a sample traffic set (ETA 30–45m).
- Marcus: monitor 5xx trend; if persists, prepare customer credit recommendation for RevOps (Lauren).
- Vanessa: prepare exec summary if customer escalates to legal/finance.

Attachments: timeline-screenshot-0518.png, nvml-stacktrace.txt

Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-05-18T11:18:00-07:00
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin Jansen <kevin.jansen@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Subject: Horizon Health — interim status & next steps (11:18 PDT)

Kevin —

Thank you for your patience and for routing traffic to the fallback region to reduce immediate impact. Short summary of what happened and what we’ve done so far:

- What happened: a recent NVML driver regression introduced kernel-level timeouts leading to repeated GPU telemetry failures, which cascaded into KV cache churn and elevated p95/p99 latency across multiple routes for Horizon Health.
- What we’ve done: rolled a canary back to the prior driver version, increased Horizon’s dedicated capacity by +2 instances, enabled prefix/KV cache warming, and applied a temporary routing policy to divert very large requests to compatible variants to reduce pressure.
- Current status: overall error rate down ~70% from peak, p95 improved but p99 still elevated for a small subset of requests. We’re continuing cache warm-up and monitoring.

Commitments:
- ETA for full recovery: we expect normal p99 within 2–3 hours barring regressions; we’ll update you if that changes.
- Credits/SLA: we will work with you and our RevOps team to assess SLA credit eligibility; Lauren will reach out separately to coordinate.
- Postmortem: we’ll share an internal RCA and a customer-friendly summary within 48 hours.

If you’d like a live update we can extend the bridge or run a short 15-minute sync — we’ll keep the bridge open for the next hour.

Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Attachments (for your team): request-sample-1678.json (sample causing elevated path), timeline-screenshot-0518.png

Kevin
